items.title: 「雙休購」爆紅與下架：一個網購平台如何撬動勞工權益討論

items.title: 習近平：從失去一切的「太子」到中國最有權勢的領導人
items.desc: 現年73歲的習近平，早已不再是那名訪美時的縣級官員。在近14年的中國領導人任期內，他改變了中國共產黨以及這個國家在世界上的地位。

items.title: 從年輕縣官到國家主席：習近平41年來的訪美影像
items.desc: 習近平即將到訪美國會晤特朗普（川普），這將是他歷來第11次以中國官方身份訪美。從31歲縣委書記到中國國家主席，BBC中文透過歷年照片，回顧他的訪美行程如何隨身份和中美關係變化。

items.title: CNN 等三家美國媒體被禁入白宮後 起訴特朗普政府

items.title: 中共五中全會日期敲定 習近平政治地位新提法成看點
items.desc: 習近平執政後的兩次六中全會，均對其政治地位作出逐層遞進的確認。本屆五中全會同樣是黨建議題，會否出現新的提法，將是全會最值得觀察的看點。

items.title: 特朗普據報將赴機場迎接習近平，待遇比肩教宗和赫魯曉夫
items.desc: 美國總統親赴機場迎接外國元首極為罕見。若不計教宗訪美的特例，這將是超過 60 年來美國總統首次以這種方式迎接他國元首。

items.title: 中國與巴基斯坦新邊界安排為何引起印度不滿？
items.desc: 中巴邊界協議挑戰印度的領土主張，也加深了印度對喀什米爾爭議地區的戰略憂慮。

items.title: 莫斯科遭到烏克蘭450架無人機襲擊，市長稱規模「迄今最大」
items.desc: 莫斯科市長稱，在夜間的襲擊中，有 450 架無人機被擊落，造成兩人死亡。

items.title: 香港首任特首董建華葬禮：規格比照霍英東 石泰峰致悼詞
items.desc: 香港回歸後首任行政長官董建華周日（9月20日）在香港舉行公祭及出殯儀式。中國國家主席習近平和多名中共政治局常委以不同形式致哀，但並未親自出席。作為首位離世的香港特首，董建華獲得的國家級治喪安排不僅是對其個人政治生涯的評價，也為未來香港前特首的身後禮遇樹立先例。

items.title: 聯合國專家：有理由相信美國在伊朗襲擊行動中犯下戰爭罪

items.title: 「運動員無法伸直雙腿睡覺」：日本亞運為何爆發住宿爭議？
items.desc: 亞運選手將入住木製貨櫃屋或一艘意大利郵輪。韓國代表團批評，貨櫃屋宿舍水管漏水，且床舖太小，運動員甚至無法伸直雙腿睡覺。

items.title: 戴安娜弟弟出書談王室 查爾斯曾稱她「很快會被遺忘」
items.desc: 戴安娜王妃逝世近30年之際，她的弟弟史賓賽伯爵出版新書，重提姐姐去世後的王室事件。他聲稱，時任王儲查爾斯曾認為戴安娜很快會被世人遺忘，但這項說法遭到王室否認。

items.title: 'UN unable to bring peace to conflicts: We haven’t seen this level of violence in decades’
items.desc: Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi is pleased to welcome Fanny Badache, Researcher at Sciences Po and Lecturer at the University of Geneva. The UN mandate is international peace and security, yet its ability to fulfill that mandate ultimately depends on the cooperation of sovereign states, namely the five powerful permanent members of the Security Council. As the UN is confronted with an increasingly fragmented, volatile and unpredictable international order, Badache argues that when those powers are divided, the mechanisms designed to enable collective security can instead produce paralysis.

items.title: US threatens South Sudan with sanctions over aid obstruction
items.desc: The United States has threatened to impose sanctions on South Sudan over alleged obstruction of humanitarian assistance, accusing officials at national, state and local levels of treating aid as a source of revenue.

items.title: Ladin: Dolomites villages refuse to give up on ancient language
items.desc: Year after year, the mountains of the Dolomites become more popular with tourists. Amid millions of visitors, 30,000 inhabitants speak a language only they understand: Ladin, one of the oldest minority languages in Europe.

items.title: Ethiopian armed groups announce anti
items.desc: On the eve of International Peace Day, an Ethiopian rebel leader announced an alliance of seven armed groups with the stated objective of toppling Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's ruling party and establishing a transitional government. The alliance consists of former enemies during the 2020 civil war that killed 600,000 people, and other armed groups from across the country, all fighting their own battles against federal troops. With the war in Sudan across the border, and several third parties like Eritrea siding with involved parties, there are fears of isolated armed conflicts in Ethiopia spilling over into a regional war. More from our correspondent Tom Canetti.

items.title: Nutrition expert shares easy steps to healthier eating
items.desc: In this edition we're looking at how to eat healthier. We speak to Cynthia Ka, the author of "Mes assiettes naturo". Cynthia says cooking is your pharmacy and doing your weekly shopping is a powerful act. We find out what her go-to recipe is and how we can all make the change to healthier eating.

items.title: New report tackles problem of governments' overreliance on consulting firms
items.desc: Dependence on consulting firms is a growing trend among governments globally. Left unchecked, it can have a negative impact due to high costs or transparency issues. Such dependence came to the fore in France a few years ago, when the Macron government was criticised for its close ties with US consulting giant McKinsey. UNESCO's Inclusive Policy Lab, headed by Iulia Sevciuc, has established a new blueprint to tackle this problem. She spoke to us in Business.

items.title: New book by Princess Diana's brother sparks royal ruckus
items.desc: A new book published Tuesday by the brother of the late Princess Diana has made headlines around the world with its damning allegations about Diana's ex-husband, now King Charles III, and reopened decades-old wounds within Britain's royal family. France 24's correspondent in London Benedicte Paviot has the details.

items.title: Macron calls on EU to tackle soaring energy prices
items.desc: Emmanuel Macron has written to the EU Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, calling on Brussels to take immediate action to lower energy prices. They have been on the rise as the conflict in the Middle East spreads, and as Ukraine's attacks on Russian diesel refineries continue.

items.title: Media ban 'an escalation even for Trump'
items.desc: CNN, MS NOW and Politico on Monday sued President Donald Trump’s administration days after they were barred from White House grounds, calling the selective ban — based on the content of their coverage — a “blatant violation” of the First Amendment. The extraordinary ban represents an escalation of Trump’s long-running efforts to restrict news coverage he finds objectionable, says France 24’s Kethevane Gorjestani.

items.title: Climate change, overfishing: Lake Chad sees fish stocks dwindle
items.desc: People living in Chad’s Lake Province are bearing the brunt of climate change. The region and the communities that have developed there have historically depended on this vast body of water. Fishing, first and foremost, but also farming, are the pillars of local livelihoods. Yet both are increasingly disrupted by erratic weather patterns: dwindling fish stocks, damaged farmland and a rising cost of living.

items.title: Trump admin's hardline deportation policy an 'attempt to break the global refugee and asylum system'
items.desc: François Picard is pleased to welcome Washington Post national security reporter Adam Taylor. The Forbidden Stories consortium, involving France 24 and 25 other media outlets, has spent six months investigating the thousands of people abruptly deported from the United States to third countries, amid concerns over due process and their ability to challenge their removal. The investigation examines how the Trump administration has made deportation a major focus of both US immigration and foreign policy.

items.title: Wars, AI and climate on agenda as world leaders meet at UN
items.desc: In the face of an unrelenting succession of global crises, this year's United Nations General Assembly has chosen as its theme “Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all”. From AI to climate change and ongoing wars, France 24 takes a look at what’s on the agenda.
